# A record written under a `for` among records is one record mapped over the
# list (lower.DataFamilies), so what it is written with is written once: the
# content of the card below cannot read `n`, and a build refuses it at the
# card rather than showing every copy the same thing. The interpreter, which
# reads the population through the same lowering, refuses it too.

! sngl generate --platform html --lang none --out out app.sngl
stderr 'app.sngl:15:17: this card is one record mapped over the `for` around it, so what it is written with is written once and cannot read n; pass what differs as a prop of the card'

! sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stderr 'cannot read n'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component card(label string, content ...component ui.node) card

component deck(cards ...component card) ui.node {
    for var c = cards {
        c.content
    }
}

component app ui.node {
    deck {
        for var n = ["a", "b"] {
            card(label=n) {
                ui.text(value=n)
            }
        }
    }
}

func testNothing(t Test, c app) {
}

ui.window {
    app
}
